page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based server instance designed for high-throughput in-memory data processing and I/O-intensive workloads. It is powered by Intel Xeon 8259CL processors running on x86_64 architecture at 3.1 GHz, delivering 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The platform is configured with 384 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Unlike diskless variants, it includes bundled local high-speed storage comprising 1800 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent mid-tier performance across parallel computation and memory-intensive operations. Multi-core compute benchmarks such as PassMark CPU (34,702.85), Geekbench multi-core (10,934.0), and stress-ng multi-core (40,658.43) place the instance within the middle 50% category. In contrast, single-thread throughput exhibits lower comparative efficiency, scoring in the bottom 25% for stress-ng single-core (1,383.49) and single-threaded gzip compression (23.37 GB/sec). Memory subsystem testing reflects uncached read bandwidth of 107.87 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 47.87 GB/sec, supporting high-rate transactional data handlers such as Redis SET operations at 37.4 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the r5dn.12xlarge delivers resource density by combining large RAM capacity, substantial NVMe scratch storage, and high networking throughput without requiring separate attached storage volume costs for transient operations. The absence of hardware GPU accelerators limits its viability for large-scale AI model generation, evidenced by modest token output on 7B LLM models (10.23 tokens/sec) and weak prompt processing on 70B models (5.77 tokens/sec). Workload fit is optimal for high-capacity in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, relational database servers, big data analytics engines, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) driven by Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processors at 3.1 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 384 GB of DDR4 RAM at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, bundled local storage of 1800 GB NVMe SSD, and 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Multi-core performance is solid across tests like PassMark CPU (34,702.85) and Geekbench multi-core (10,934.0), though single-threaded metrics reflect modest performance. The instance achieves 37.4 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and uncached memory read throughput of 107.87 GB/sec. Combining high RAM density, rapid local storage, and wide network channels without GPU acceleration, the r5dn.12xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, caching tiers, data analytics, and transaction-heavy relational systems.
